admin-api.description: The operator's HTTP API: the composition, conversations, transcripts, live events, messages, abort and reset; serves the dashboard's built files. On Cloudflare the Worker serves it, reaching each conversation's Durable Object and listing them from an index.

admin-auth-token.description: Who is an operator: a request carrying the bearer token PIKIT_ADMIN_TOKEN. What admin routes (the dashboard) ask before answering.

channel-http.description: Talk to an agent over HTTP: send a message, get the answer in the response.

channel-telegram.description: Talk to your agent in Telegram: send your bot a message, get the answer in the chat.

channel-telegram-webhook.description: Talk to your agent in Telegram when it runs on Cloudflare: Telegram posts each message to your Worker.

conversations-file.description: The conversation registry in one JSON file: which Pi session each conversation is in now.

conversations-kv.description: The conversation registry in storage.kv: which Pi session each conversation is in now, on a server or in a Durable Object.

credentials-file.description: The model providers' credentials in one JSON file, readable only by its owner (mode `0600`).

deployment-cloudflare.description: Runs a pikit project on Cloudflare: the Worker and its Durable Objects running the project's two Apps, wrangler.jsonc, and the commands `pikit up | down | logs | status | dev` delegate to.

deployment-docker.description: Runs a pikit project in Docker on a server: the image, the container, the process entrypoint, its logs, and the commands `pikit up | down | restart | logs | status` delegate to.

execution-do.description: The agent's workspace and shell inside its Durable Object, on Cloudflare: files in the object's SQL, a bash without processes, git with fenced pushes, and node in QuickJS.

execution-local.description: The agent's tools work on this server: its filesystem and its shell.

extension-house-rules.description: House rules for the agents that name them: the rules in config as a system prompt section, and the tools in config refused before they run.

health-registry.description: What is up, degraded or down: components report their own state; /health fails when an essential one stays down, so the supervisor restarts the process.

log-events.description: One structured log line per operational event: what reached which agent, how each run ended, how long it took and what it cost.

mailbox-local.description: Hands a channel's message to the actor that owns its conversation, in the same app: actor.mailbox and actor.inbox on a server.

outbound-durable.description: Every answer is stored before it is sent, then delivered in order per conversation, retried, and sent again after a crash.

platform-cloudflare.description: Reaches each conversation's Durable Object from the Worker, and wakes components in it on its one alarm: actor.mailbox, actor.inbox and wakeups on Cloudflare.

provider-anthropic.description: Anthropic's Claude models for your agents. An agent names one as `anthropic/<modelId>`, for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`.

provider-faux.description: Fake models for tests only, with no network, key or cost: `faux/echo` answers `faux: <your message>`; `faux/scripted` calls a tool when told `call: <tool> <json>` and shows the system prompt it got (`echo-system`).

provider-openrouter.description: The models OpenRouter serves, for your agents. An agent names one as `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>`, for example `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.

router-basic.description: Every message goes to one agent: `defaultAgent`.

router-rules.description: Each conversation goes to the agent of the first rule in config it matches.

runtime-pi.description: The agent runtime: Pi runs your agents, and this component plugs it into the app.

secrets-cloudflare.description: Secrets from the Worker's env on Cloudflare: its secrets and variables, never its bindings.

server-bun.description: The HTTP server of the server target: Hono on `Bun.serve`.

storage-do.description: The app's SQL database (storage.sql) in a Durable Object's own SQLite, on Cloudflare: records each conversation's object keeps.

storage-kv-sql.description: Small JSON values each component keeps across restarts, by key, in a namespace of its own: storage.kv on the app's SQL database.

storage-sqlite.description: The app's SQL database (storage.sql) in one SQLite file, through node:sqlite: records components keep across restarts.

tool-bash.description: Pi's own `bash` tool, for the agents that name it: it runs a shell command in the working directory and returns its output (the last lines when it is long), with an optional timeout.

tool-edit.description: Pi's own `edit` tool, for the agents that name it: it replaces exact pieces of text in a file, each one unique in it.

tool-fetch.description: The `fetch` tool, for the agents that name it: one HTTP(S) request to a web page or an API, with HTML as readable text and links, JSON pretty-printed, and binary content refused.

tool-mcp.description: The tools of remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP), for the agents that name them: each tool named in config becomes the agent tool <server>_<tool>.

tool-read.description: Pi's own `read` tool, for the agents that name it: it reads a text file (from a line, up to a number of lines) or an image, and truncates long files for the model.

tool-websearch-brave.description: The `websearch` tool, for the agents that name it: searches the web with the Brave Search API, whose key the model never sees.

tool-write.description: Pi's own `write` tool, for the agents that name it: it creates or overwrites a file, creating its parent directories.

wakeups-timers.description: Wakes your components at the time they ask for, retrying failed handlers: wakeups as in-process timers on a server.

workspace-local.description: Each agent's tools work in a directory of their own on this server: order, not isolation.
